num_flights.method: count of stair_rise-type dimensions (DIM02, DIM05, DIM09, DIM13, DIM16, DIM20, DIM22), each spanning a distinct FFL range
num_flights.notes: 7 flights between the roof (602.402/602.307 F.F.L.) and the lowest floor level (589.218 F.F.L.).

num_risers_total.method: sum of step_formula.count across the 7 stair_rise dimensions: 15+7+14+12+12+14+5
num_risers_total.notes: Cross-check: 79 risers at their respective heights sum to 13185mm, matching DIM12's printed 13184 (1mm rounding) and the FFL-based total_vertical_drop.

riser_height.method: dominant/typical riser height across flights; not a single uniform figure
riser_height.notes: 6 of 7 flights (DIM05, 09, 13, 16, 20, 22; 64 risers) use 165mm. Only the top flight (DIM02, 15 risers) uses 175mm.

num_treads_total.notes: Standard convention (each flight's top riser lands on a landing/floor with no corresponding tread). Not independently labeled on the drawing.

tread_length.method: estimated for flight 1 only: horizontal run = sqrt(diagonal^2 - rise^2) using DIM04 (3780mm diagonal) and DIM02 (2625mm rise) = ~2720mm; going = run / 14 treads
tread_length.notes: Only flight 1 has a diagonal dimension (DIM04) to back-calculate a horizontal run from; flights 2-7 have no diagonal/horizontal run dimension in this section. Geometric estimate, not a labeled tread-going figure -- a plan view would give this directly.

total_tread_length.method: not derivable -- only flight 1 (DIM04) has a diagonal dimension to back-calculate a horizontal run from; flights 2-7 have no diagonal or horizontal run dimension in this section view
total_tread_length.notes: Flight 1's estimated horizontal run is ~2720mm (see tread_length). The total across all 7 flights needs horizontal/plan dimensions not present in this drawing.

num_landings.method: flights - 1, assuming a single continuous switchback run between the top and bottom floor levels
num_landings.notes: Ambiguous: elevation datums include near-duplicate levels 596.623 vs 596.313 (likely one physical landing referenced twice) and a medium-confidence T.O.C. +597.06 datum that may indicate an additional, unlabeled landing. DIM05's flight rise (1155mm, 599.770->596.623) doesn't match the raw FFL difference between those two references (3147mm), suggesting an intermediate landing not captured as its own dimension.

total_vertical_drop.notes: Matches DIM12's printed label (13184) and the sum of all 7 flights' riser rises (2625+1155+2310+1980+1980+2310+825=13185; 1mm rounding).
